text: The treesages told Veneda that the hand that brought down the Unknighted One will be her end too, so she set out to destroy the Heart-weald. Deep inside, she fears you.
You heard how Veneda forced people and amberspawn to live together in one city. They kept fighting, many left, and much of the city burned down deserted.
In the Amberqueen’s private chambers you found a wedding gown with symbols of eastern and western Avalon uniting, and Veneda’s tome of amber magic.
You overheard Veneda tell the coven that uniting Venedia is only the first step: as a Queen of Ruin she means to unite the west and lead her army against Tuathan.
Aedh or the Twins were crowned in Lothian, but Claudyne the Unknighted burst through the rosette above the throne in the middle of the ceremony.
Olfrid was crowned queen of Lothian, but Claudyne the Unknighted burst through the rosette above the throne in the middle of the ceremony.
Your evidence secured the throne of Lothian for young Eldrid, with Hilbrid at her side.
Your amberspawn drew Veneda’s herd away from her during the sabbath. The Amberqueen lost control of her creatures.
With the essence in hand, you head with the Fore-dweller to the walls of Tuathan. Valeska reminds him that he owes the Blackwood.
Nonus was freed from the Cradle’s grip and, with Caprellida at his side, is ready to put right what he has done.
The Fomorian senate agreed, at a high price, to keep the Slavepath open for freed slaves, but runaways will be punished more harshly.
You reached the strange land of the Cradle with the Fore-dweller, but he senses that you are too late.
You poured the essences of the Kings of Ruin into the Voracity. The Fore-dweller lost his chance and turned on you.
At the Cradle, other Fore-dwellers stepped out from behind the pillars, or you left Tuathan for eastern Avalon to wait for the Once and Future King.
You are back in Colonia Mariana: the Fallen Spire now stands in the landscape, Nonus has vanished, and the Fore-dwellers were driven back.
On an old battlefield you found Nonus’s war banner, discarded under rusty armour.
A Firbolg deciphered a letter to Marius (Nonus): its author misses him and suffers under the harsh Octavia.
You found Saeric, Nonus’s former slave, and showed him the titulus from Nonus’s villa.
You found Selachius, the author of the letter to Nonus, wyrded and broken.
In Nonus’s untouched house you found a hidden compartment behind a creaking wall.
Arkona turned away from the Amberqueen: its gates are closed to her and its warriors went home.
Varegaard took Perungrad back from Veneda’s people and keeps his word to support the Blackwood Alliance.
Vlinsk declared against the Amberqueen, and its grain will feed the rebellion.
The hut herder gave you the huts, and Valeska’s emissaries led them to the mountain path for the Blackwood Alliance.
In Sorlois you found a heap of glowing stones like those built into Castle Lothian, with wheelbarrows left beside them.
You filled the gaps in the unfinished junction with luminescent stones.
You piled luminescent stones along the walls and next to both entrances.
You hauled the glowstones away from the twin temples.
A Fomorian magistrate prepared your travel permits and warned you that the province is drowning in discord between Octavia and Nonus.
You got a hunting permit from the Firbolg forest rangers.
A slave child brought you to senator Culpean, who is looking for capable mercenaries.
At the Bona Dea feast you agreed on whom to bring down: Caprellida’s seat in the senate or Octavia’s Deep One title.
You entered the senate with representatives of the runaway slaves to negotiate with the Fomorians.
Following the song through a red filter, you found a human girl asleep in a cage on the fells.
You armed the people of the Preserve, the human city held by the Fomorians.
You saved a traveler from the flames, leaving his cart behind.
You solved the mystery of the boy’s “curse” at the hair-cutting ceremony, and his mother thanked you with Blessed Mead.
You helped the people here, and your deed is marked on the map.
You asked the old man on the trail for a change in your fate. He vanished, and something changed for the better.
You let the runaways keep the goods they had stolen from you.
At a market high above the ground, you met a sad girl who has never touched the grass below and asked you what it feels like.
You fed Askold, a blinded Venedian knyaz who lost everything on the Night of the Amber Moon, when the women of the rulers revealed themselves as Veneda’s Coven.
A man fleeing the Heart-weald warned you that the witch queen defaced the treesages and they went mad.
You met a wounded Fomorian fugitive in the forest and either turned him in for the reward or helped him escape north.
Halfway up the tower, a silent Fore-dweller grew chairs out of the wyrdstone floor and sat down with you.
Two ragged humans bumped into you in the street and ran off with part of your belongings.
On the battlefield, a Fomorian child brought you a message: his friends want to meet you.
In the camp, people stared at your black goat, and an old soldier warned you that it is no animal and brings misfortune.
You met a man and his son fleeing the town oppressed by the Fomorians, and either brought them back or helped them on their way.
From the overlook you fired upon the brigands of the Wagenburg with your new crossbow.
You let a terror-inducing candle burn upwind of the Wagenburg.
With fake wounds and an illusion of the white wyrdbear, you sowed panic inside the Wagenburg.
Underwater at the foot of the cliff, you stirred up a storm that threatened the Wagenburg.
You made someone pay a grim price: Askold agreed to become a “sweet saint”, or a Fomorian cut off his own hand as proof for Octavia.
You attacked Nonus while he was distracted, or talked a desperate stranger into becoming a “sweet saint” for the bees.
You won the fight against the uprising.
You raised an ordinary amber egg before the crowd, claiming it is the weapon Veneda fears. The lie worked.
You set Veneda’s palace in Arkona on fire. Many died, including the steward, Knyaz Askold’s wife.
You escaped the pursuing Kingseekers, setting the Hanging Trail ablaze or leading them into the giant hive.
You freed the black goat, and it has followed you ever since.
Kendrick the Ghostly Scholar joined you, though he has his own research to do.
You accepted the Candle Golem as your companion.
Isolut, the woman you met during the festival in Colonia Mariana, joined you.
You followed a mysterious shadow and found inhuman footprints and a glint of gold in the mud.
You found something of value in the southeastern corner of the lake.
The hermit’s hut by the lake stood empty, his things neatly left behind. You took what he left.
The family from the windmill, reunited with their lost daughter, moved out and left you a note of thanks and a reward.
You searched through the valuables people discarded in desperation.
With the knight gone, you studied the gate or opened it.
In the barbican wall you found a Sorlois stone carved with part of an old map leading to southeastern Lothian. The rest is missing.
In a mansion at the heart of Sorlois you found an old bedroll left by treasure hunters and an irregular glowstone.
Under the tower, the blue filter showed collapsed tunnels like roots, where you found a small relic.
The family in the windmill met their fate, or you made the woman a new candle to keep them safe.
You climbed the Slavepath and heard from the fugitives that the Fore-dwellers attacked the Fomorians and the slaves seized the moment to escape.
Octavia asked you to join her fight against Nonus, the traitor Marius.
Caprellida, unmasked in a small office, asked for your help against the most formidable being in the province.
You passed Caprellida’s respects to Nonus. He dismissed her, though something in him changed, and left.
You went to meet your Fore-dweller ally at the Fallen Spire, which split a mountainside of the Somber Ridge.
The politician confirmed your deal about Cymothius: your reward waits at an arena in eastern Colonia Mariana.
You left the cursed latifundia, fearing what Nonus himself can do if his followers can change the weather.
You told Caprellida that Nonus asked about her, and she agreed to an alliance: she wants Nonus back in politics instead of chasing godhood.
Under the ruined chapter house you found a scared acolyte hiding from the Amber Coven, which raided the place.
You helped the acolyte bury the dead priests. She paid you with a large piece of amber the Coven left in the oldest priest’s mouth.
Refugees at the rapids told you that Veneda is just to the north, overseeing the burning of Zheremie, the wooden city on the water that resisted her longest.
Fleeing Veneda into the western forest, you were hidden by Orlof, a weald-priest, and asked him how to stand against her.
Your Blessed Mead let Orlof wake the treesage, and he promised to help a fellow enemy of the Amberqueen.
You sank the harbour chain, and Varegaard’s sea raiders stormed the pier and overran the surprised garrison.
Gerdwyn turned her back on the Ironwall Brigade or disbanded it, ending its tainted legacy.
Gerdwyn decided to return to the Lothian camp after her travels and lead the Ironwall Brigade.
Osbert accepted the title of Knyaz of Vlinsk and set out again, knowing he has a home to return to.
Osbert renounced his claim to Vlinsk and chose the open road.
Lyssa and Cai decided to go back with Elgan and rebuild the old workshop in Lothian as a family.
Elgan let Lyssa and Cai stay in their new Fomorian workshop; he will visit whenever he can.
After Iunis defeated Cymothius in the arena, the whole of Colonia Mariana talks of her show.
Iunis defeated Cymothius in the arena. Officially it was his penalty for high treason.
Gerdwyn’s epilogue: the fate of the Ironwall Brigade and of Gerdwyn after the journey.
Osbert’s epilogue: how he spent his years after the journey.
Elgan’s epilogue: his candle workshop after the journey.
You told Claudyne that Sorlois was always a mirage kept alive by his pride, and your words struck home.
You reminded Claudyne of his sister Elinor, who waited in vain for him at Saint Micah’s Mount.
You told Claudyne that his Oval Table failed because he made knights into champions, while Arthur made champions into knights.
You told Claudyne that his wars with the other Kings of Ruin, not Lothian’s rulers, brought about the Fall of Lothian.
You followed the aqueduct to its source in the mountains and found the water there no more wyrded than at the other end.
In old accounts you learned that the old king of the Aquileans took the rest of the court and the royal heirlooms to Saint Micah’s Mount instead of following Arthur.
You overheard Claudyne condemn the knights of his Oval Table one by one, or saw him standing over old foundations north of the castle.
The wild tribes told you how Claudyne’s wars with the other Kings of Ruin destroyed their waystones and drove them toward Lothian.
You watched a young priest, Mardigan, set off on a penitent journey to a faraway shrine.
You sensed that old Loth is not just angry about the road: he fears the forest.
A former castle guard told you that King Loth had him secretly guard a woman prisoner in rooms under the southern tower.
You watched a man call down the rope ladder at the waterfall, but caught only fragments of the password.
The archivist of Sorlois told you about his library and how the city bound him to it.
In a calm glade you found a bench fit for a human and a Fomorian side by side, and large crustacean tracks.
Senator Caprellida spoke of Nonus with admiration: in her eyes he is the hero Fomoria needs.
The treesage told you an old story of a spurned girl who found the amber-bound chrysalis on the shore and learned to awaken sleeping things.
You followed the crooked woman to her hut in the woods. Up close, she is just a very tall old woman.
You worked out how the king (or Aedh) was killed: someone familiar came at night, talked with him, and strangled him.
In a dream you were a black-haired slave girl bought from the Fomorians for her resemblance to someone, dressed in white and taken north.
Behind the secret entrance you found a luxurious cell for a prisoner of great value, with marks etched on the wall.
The archivist confirmed that the tome of flesh magic came from his archive and that Olfrid’s agents sought it years ago.
You declared that the Dolorous Twins should rule Lothian, though the common folk fear them.
You declared that Aedh should be king, though the sheriff warned that the secrets of his past may yet come to light.
You declared that Queen Olfrid should stay in charge, though she has no heir and refuses to use that accursed magic again.
You declared that Hilbrid’s daughter should rule Lothian; the document making Hilbrid queen is legal and valid.
In a ruined townhouse you found a wild geese nest full of eggs.
In the remains of the camp you collected dried fish, and heard a desperate scream from the nearby grove.
In one of the cages you found a dusty object and scattered coins.
You pulled a large piece of bog oak out of the hillside, a wood craftspeople value.
You broke out warm stones radiating strange energy.
You searched the valuables left behind when the castle was evacuated.
In an abandoned cellar you found a barrel of dried fish.
Under the floorboards of a larger home you found something valuable.
The blue filter showed you ripples in the air, and under them two buried caches with items from Sorlois.
You found a tree hollow full of enormous pine nuts and gathered them before the owner came back.
You looted the battlefield strewn with old corpses and those massacred by Nonus, and found something usable.
At the Cradle, five Fore-dwellers stepped out from behind the pillars to confront your ally, and you chose whether to take his side.
You toppled one of the ancient columns around the pool.
You found Claudyne’s magnificent war banner with the Aquilean crest, which may wake his old memories.
You pieced together Veneda’s Venedian wedding cloak, blending Pendragon and Venedian heraldry, once torn apart by someone of great strength.
In the ash you found a coral idol of a sea god whose face was scrubbed off and replaced with a Fomorian visage.
You led Claudyne against another King of Ruin. He was beaten back and retreated, and his rival was weakened too.
You led Veneda against another King of Ruin. She was beaten back and retreated, and her rival was weakened too.
You led Nonus against another King of Ruin. He was beaten back and retreated, and his rival was weakened too.
You bandaged a wounded Fomorian fugitive and sent him north.
You let the Fomorian in the grotto go instead of handing him to Octavia, with or without taking a bloody proof.
You set your enslaved Fomorians free.
You bought a family of four human slaves free and paid a captain to take them to King’s Pass.
You let the runaways go.
You gave the man and his son supplies and showed them the safest way to the Slavepath.
The rebels won: the latifundium burned and its cages were broken, and their leaders asked you to help them negotiate.
In the senate, the Fomorians agreed at a high price to keep the Slavepath open for freed slaves, but will punish runaways more harshly.
You helped fix a wagon axle and learned that the waystone at the top of King’s Pass is still broken and that exiled King Loth is there.
Your lucky roll won Aedh a pot paid from his father’s coffers, saving him great embarrassment.
You delivered Knyaz Askold’s words to his wife and daughter, who now regret siding with the Amberqueen.
The man in the black mask accepted what you brought and let you in.
You tried to stop the bandits’ plot against Ailena’s wedding. Either way, the wedding is off.
You told King Loth about Queen Olfrid’s request. He believes she dabbles in dark magic and paid you.
You told King Loth about Aedh’s request. He thinks his son has started scheming behind his back, and paid you.
You told King Loth about the Twins’ request. He shrugged it off and paid you.
You turned away from the Ironwall Brigade, or sold Rolf the location of the treasure of Sorlois in exchange for peace with the Southlanders.
You gave Octavia something precious that belonged to Nonus, so she would hand Iunis her prey.
You told the people of Vlinsk that the “noonwraith” in the fields was Mladena, who escaped her punishment. They caught her and agreed to a fair trial.
You barged into the wagon and saw the Dolorous Twins, King Loth’s children, joined at the torso.
You asked King Loth why he is afraid, and he exploded with anger.
You searched the road to the castle, strewn with things the Lothians left behind when they fled years ago.
Rolf defeated you and had you thrown out of the Ironwall Brigade’s camp.
Your trickery at the sabbath was exposed. You fled, and the Amber Coven will never let you back.
Isolut, the woman you met during the festival in Colonia Mariana, joined you.
Isolut cooked you a dinner of monotropa, and you either ate it with a smile or told her how it grows.
On watch, you either told Isolut to face the dangers around her or dreamed with her about the mountains.
You kept Isolut away from the Firbolg “celebration”, or went with her and let her see what it really was.
Isolut tried to feed the skinsacks. You either let her learn the hard way or killed them first.
Back at the ruined spire, Isolut was waiting for you by her campfire.
Back at the ruined spire, Isolut was waiting for you by her campfire, still seeing the world her own way.
You told Kendrick he has been dead for a long time. He refused to believe it.
You told Kendrick again that he is dead. He is less sure of himself this time.
Under Isidor’s hut you found the hidden study Kendrick marked on your map, with a skeleton among cracked pieces of amber.
You told Kendrick that Gnezdo was destroyed years ago, and he insisted you must be in the wrong place.
You told Kendrick he must have been here over a hundred years ago. You searched for his lost friend Rootseer in vain.
You told Kendrick that his visit here must have been centuries ago, and a hint of doubt crept into his voice.
You told Kendrick that you just saw him die. He would have none of it.
In the reliquary you found a tangle of white stone fingers with red veins, a relic somehow tied to the waystones.
Kendrick showed you on an old sketch of the sewers of Colonia Mariana the hidden headquarters of the Lothian spies.
You tried to help the wounded Kealan down to the pier, but the ship left without you.
You offered dried fish to the fox with bells in its tail. It ate and vanished into the mists, and something changed.
The fox accepted your offering again, looking healthier. You suspect it may be one of the minor spirits that came from the Homelands.
The fox accepted your offering, its tail of talismans floating above it.
The fox accepted your offering among others left for it, its paws no longer touching the ground.
The fox floated around you with joy, more pleased with your presence than with the offering.
You won the trust of the people at the windmill, or the boy looking for his sister Alysa told you she went after a strange band west of here.
You faced the angry ghosts at the forgotten cemetery, abandoned by their kin almost a decade ago.
The spirits of the abandoned courtyard turned to you, calling Loth no true king and asking you to lead them east.
Iunis hurled insults at the arrogant Fore-dweller on the wall in his own language.
The denizens of Sorlois told you why their city is the best place to live and gave you a farewell gift.
You persuaded the Southlander Elder Council to return to the Lothian crown, and their envoys set out for the castle.
The bees want a “sweet saint”: you either lay down for one to sting you, or they asked you to find someone willing.
You solved the treesages’ final riddle, the first since the Amberqueen to do so, and won a prize from their hoard.
You debated philosophy with the treesages for an hour or two.
The hermit admitted that you saw him in the golden reflection, and told you of the day he left his brothers for a shrine near Four Maidens.
Claudyne the Unknighted broke through the gate into your world, and you faced him while he was still confused.
Claudyne stepped back from you, studied you for a moment, and walked away into the wyrdness.
The living stone fingers of the relic touched the runes on the portcullis, and the keep’s gate opened.
The treasures of Sorlois are yours. You took the heavy Aquilean crown as proof and set off back to Castle Lothian.
The Southlanders are at peace with the Lothian crown and the Ironwall Brigade’s raids are over.
You won an important fight.
You held out against Nonus. Surprised, he spoke in human words and withdrew, calling you something other than human, Fomorian or Fore-dweller.
The brigands of the Wagenburg block the way to the Pass and demand an ounce of gold per head, far more than you can pay.
Iunis found a cliff over the bay under part of the Wagenburg, which a Fomorian sea ritual could bring down.
Varegaard offered to support your cause by retaking Perungrad from the Amberqueen, if you find a way past the iron chain that guards the port at night.
Under the rubble in Sorlois you found a dead Lothian architect’s scroll case with sketches of the city and a letter from Claudyne meant for Arthur.
In a study you found a giant model of Sorlois, with many buildings never built and a giant statue of Claudyne.
You ate a vile old broth and got its recipe, or Gerdwyn studied the old battlefield to learn why the Fomorians won.
Senator Culpean asked you to meet him at The First Step, where he needs someone with sharp senses.
On the beach, Kendrick told you about lands now sunk under the sea, whose traces are preserved in the amber found here.
The ghost of a traveling midwife told Elgan the story of her life in a dream and left him some of her skills.
The ghost of a gloomy trailkeeper told Gerdwyn the story of his life in a dream and left her some of his skills.
The ghost of an ancient mariner told Osbert the story of his life in a dream and left him some of his skills.
The ghost of a blind squire told Iunis the story of her life in a dream and left her some of her skills.
You lit a candle by the totem of a traveling midwife.
You lit a candle by the totem of a gloomy trailkeeper.
You lit a candle by the totem of an ancient mariner.
You lit a candle by the totem of a blind squire.
Osbert performed for the people of the wagonfort and was paid for it.
Osbert performed in the Archtown for an audience that responded to every joke and ballad as never before.
Osbert performed and learned something new, perhaps for the Fomorian researchers at the latifundia.
Osbert performed in the courtyard of Castle Lothian for servants, builders and knights.
South of the castle, Elgan walks his old trail: his workshop is half a day’s march away.
In the workshop’s accounting book, Elgan found his wife’s handwriting continuing long after his own stopped.
Gerdwyn exposed Rolf’s lies, or saved a supporter from his henchmen, and the camp split into a fight.
Gerdwyn advised the officers of the Ironwall Brigade to stop raiding the Southlanders.
Gerdwyn left the camp of the Ironwall Brigade, either walking away from it or setting out on a quest for revenge.
Elgan’s clue leads to the Fomorian Province: a Fomorian who wore a tunic with two sea snakes and an anchor.
Iunis met a friend from the arena, or Osbert handed over the deed to save Clyfar, who escaped.
In the artisan district, Elgan found a shop that once belonged to a candlemaker.
Iunis gave the Fore-dweller Octavia’s message. It agreed to meet her at the eastern feet of the Somber Ridge.
Gerdwyn negotiated the Brigade’s surrender and sent the survivors to rejoin the camp in Lothian.
Gerdwyn negotiated the Brigade’s surrender, disbanded it and shared out its treasury.
Gerdwyn told the officers she will return to lead the Brigade in Lothian after her travels.
Gerdwyn told the officers she will return to the Lothian camp as its scout and guide after her travels.
Elgan found the street where his family lives in Colonia Mariana, far from the squalid districts.
You told Caprellida what you uncovered about Octavia near Tuathan, though you had little proof.
You told Caprellida what you uncovered about Octavia near Tuathan, with some proof to back it.
You told Caprellida what you uncovered about Octavia near Tuathan, with solid proof.
You armed the slaves of Octavia’s villa, who are ready to rise.
You found the masked rebels in the alleys of Colonia Mariana, passed them word from the rebellion’s leaders and gave them money.
In the arena, Iunis finally stood face to face with Cymothius, who had gladiatrices banned from the colosseum.
Magnus confessed that he took his waystone from a frontier village and people died; the bandits came for revenge.
Thick wyrdness fell over all of Venedia, and people boarded up their homes. Veneda’s army will be caught by surprise.
The priest rewarded you with Blessed Mead, one of the rarest goods in Avalon.
You told Isolut to keep her eyes on the dangers around her. She did, with a tear under her mask.
You told Isolut that monotropa grows on human bodies. She buried the dead and asked never to talk about it again.
You took Isolut to the Firbolg “celebration”, and she saw what it really was.
You let Isolut try to feed the skinsacks and saved her when they attacked.
You joined King Loth’s huge, slow expedition back to Lothian; many of its people still fear the road ahead.
You rebuilt the lumberyard by the border of Straywood.
You rebuilt the watermill.
The main areas of Castle Lothian were restored with your help.
You built fortifications against whatever comes out of Straywood.
You built fortifications on the northern side.
You built fortifications farther out.
You built fortifications among the flooded ruins on the plains toward Sorlois.
You pulled a young woman in a gilded half-mask out of the water and either let her join you or sent her on her way east.
You walked through the Fomorian victory celebration, with Fore-dwellers’ heads on posts and contempt in every stare.
You tried to snatch the purse.
In the chest you found the gagged commander of the Wagenburg, cast out by the brigands. You spared him and he fled.
You smashed the Fore-dweller statue and drew strange power from it, until a vengeful spirit rose from the rubble.
The hut herder told you that the Coven abandoned their walking huts after the Night of the Amber Moon and he was hired to round them up.
You let Valeska and the Fore-dweller fight it out, and both were wounded.
You fought your way past the Timesworn Sentinel.
With the sabbath in full swing, you slipped away while Veneda and the Coven’s leaders talked in the stone circle.
You accused King Loth of murder before the royal family and the sheriff, and convinced at least some of them.
Queen Olfrid was found dead in her tent, and you inspected the scene or left it to the sheriff.
Prince Aedh was found dead in his tent, and you inspected the scene or left it to the sheriff.
You insisted that Aedh pay for his crimes. He was jailed for fratricide and high treason.
You are a guest at the ceremony of the kingdom’s restitution in the rebuilt Castle Lothian.
At the bottom of the water you found an old coin press and unstamped precious metal discs.
You came away with something from a hiding place whose owner nearly caught you.
You took something useful from a ghostly ritual battlefield, or from an abandoned camp’s stores.
You dug up a black iron casket for senator Culpean. His guards took it, and he paid you well to leave.
You combed the shore for an amber egg and found only tiny pieces of amber. Large eggs are hard to come by.
You reached for an object in the bushes, and a Babay sprang out.
On the shore you found an amber egg big enough to pass for the one that hatched before your eyes, to show in Zheremie.
The blue filter led you to a hidden lookout above King’s Pass with an old fire pit and things left behind.
Following Kendrick’s sketch, you found the Lothian spies’ hideout under Colonia Mariana, with coins and a lockbox.
Gerdwyn met Toke, an old axeman of the Ironwall Brigade who was like a grandfather to her and thought she was dead.
You refused to fight, and the priest sentenced you to hang from a nobleman’s runewagon at King’s Pass.
An old woman told you the statue is Saint Hilbrid, Queen Olfrid’s kind younger sister, whom the common folk of Lothian hail as a saint.
You learned that Nonus cares for his Fomorian people and hates the Fore-dwellers, and that senator Caprellida backs him against Octavia.
A girl told you the forbidden story of the twin sisters Radmila and Mladena: Mladena killed her sister over a young man and was sentenced to drowning.
Vlinsk stopped its harvest: everyone fears the noonwraith in the fields that nearly scared the farmer Andri to death.
Among the scribbles you found a note to Caedr: something was hidden in the wyrdness west of the old milepost.
The priest asked you to help an acolyte carrying something the Amberqueen hunts to reach Zheremie, and gave you the secret words for her.
The weald-priest told you that only someone who knows every part of you could reshape you to your former self.
You told the woman in the windmill that her candle does not work.
You questioned the girl hiding in the fields. She asked you not to tell the villagers about her.
You rounded up the walking huts into the herder’s corral, and he rewarded you.
You watched Bielobog and Chernobog take shape out of white light and black tendrils, embrace, and vow to destroy each other.
Under Isidor’s hut you found a hidden study full of amber, a skeleton among cracked pieces like eggshells.
You reported to the Dolorous Twins what you saw, and they were pleased.
You accepted a secret request from Queen Olfrid, who keeps something like an alchemical laboratory in her tent.
You accepted the Dolorous Twins’ request and took their dripping doll into the forest.
Prince Aedh gave you a delicate task near Castle Lothian, to be kept from his parents.
The quartermaster warned you to watch your back around King Loth, who has borrowed heavily for years on the promise of rebuilding Lothian.
Watching the doll, you saw a wyrd-warped child of ten or twelve come to sniff at it.
You dug up the grave for Aedh and found a gold bracelet from Aquilea beside a black-haired woman’s bones.
You brought Queen Olfrid the tome she lost when the court left Lothian.
Aedh found that the bracelet is a fake and wonders where the real one is.
You paid for the Firbolgs’ dam, and one of them told you his names: Dancing Reed and Dirt Under Fingernails.
Following the song through a red filter, you found a human girl asleep in a cage on the fells.
The wyrdglass led you to a hidden basement in the ruined city, full of instruments and notes untouched since its fall.
You joined the song of the guardians and walked past them into the lair of their father.
You stole silverware from a market stall. The market will be on guard now.
You looted a merchant’s cart someone hid in the wyrdness.
You took the small offerings from the forgotten graves.
You cheated on the decisive roll in Aedh’s dice game.
You took the offerings from the statue’s bowl, and someone ran off into the ruins.
You dug up a black iron chest with an artifact and valuables.
You tried to get the merchant’s jewelry back from the water sprites.
